text.en: Every cell needs oxygen, a blood supply and a way to remove waste. Respiration, transport and excretion handle these jobs.

Respiration breaks down glucose to release energy stored as ATP. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen: glucose gives CO2 + water + energy.
Anaerobic respiration happens without oxygen: in yeast it gives ethanol and CO2, and in our muscles it gives lactic acid, which causes cramps.
In humans air passes through the nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea and bronchi to alveoli, where gas exchange happens. Haemoglobin carries oxygen.
The human heart has four chambers and gives double circulation. Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood do not mix.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood to it. Capillaries exchange materials with tissues.
In plants, xylem carries water and minerals upward using transpiration pull, and phloem carries food in both directions, called translocation.
Excretion removes nitrogenous wastes. In humans the kidneys filter blood in nephrons, forming urine that passes through the ureter to the bladder.
In kidney failure, haemodialysis acts as an artificial kidney. Plants excrete through leaves, resins and gums.

problem.en: Why do athletes get muscle cramps after heavy exercise?

text.en: In heavy exercise oxygen supply is low, so pyruvate is converted anaerobically.
Lactic acid builds up in the muscles.

prompt.en: How do respiration, transport and excretion work?

points.en: Aerobic respiration gives much more energy than anaerobic.
The heart has four chambers and double circulation.
Kidneys filter blood; nephron is the unit.
